title: Council backs high performance aquatic centre exploration
subtitle: Also covered: delegation of authority by-law, road safety and traffic calming plan, tariff response update, micromobility agreement extension.
overview: Council passed a notice of motion from the Mayor to explore a high performance aquatic centre with a 50 metre competition pool, practice pool, training spaces and spectator seating {{vote:m6}}. It directs staff to consider the facility when planning west-side recreation options, asks the Mayor to write to federal and provincial ministers about funding, and commits the City to work with regional partners. The City's participation depends on confirmed senior-government and partner funding. The Mayor said it would not affect the property tax levy in the near term.

Council also approved a new Delegation of Authority By-law {{vote:m3}}. It reorganizes who may sign documents and adds authority to sign grant agreements for the multi-unit residential acquisition program. Council extended the shared micromobility agreement {{vote:m2}}.

Council received two reports for information: the road safety and traffic calming plan {{vote:m4}} and the update on the 10-point U.S. tariff response plan {{vote:m5}}. Staff said a broader plan for school-zone traffic calming will come to Council after the province's decision to end automated speed enforcement. Council also heard announcements recognizing a renal program anniversary and a walk to raise awareness of gender-based violence.

decisions.detail: Council directed that any future indoor aquatic centre costing include a 50 metre competition pool, asked the Mayor to seek federal and provincial funding, and asked staff to consider the facility in west-side recreation planning {{vote:m6}}.
Council approved a new by-law, replacing the 2017 by-law, that reorganizes signing authority by type of document and adds authority for grant agreements {{vote:m3}}.

Council approved the extension and authorized the Commissioner of Integrated Planning and Public Works to sign the amendment and future agreements, subject to the City Solicitor's satisfaction {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Road safety and traffic calming plan
decisions.detail: Council received the 2025 road safety countermeasures and traffic calming implementation plan for information {{vote:m4}}.
Council received the implementation update on the 10-point tariff response plan for information {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Delegates from swim, artistic swimming and sport-hosting groups said current pools are oversubscribed, with long waitlists. They said aging pools face shutdowns, and that athletes travel outside the region to train and compete.

Delegates and councillors argued a 50 metre facility could bring sport tourism through hosting meets. A delegate said senior-government funding is essential and that being project-ready helps secure it.

Councillors raised concerns about operating costs and the limits of the local tax base. One suggested a shared operating model with partners and a mix of community and high performance use, and noted pressure on funding from higher levels of government.

A councillor asked how a facility would serve para swimmers. A delegate said accessibility should be designed in across the pool, deck and change rooms. A councillor also stressed that a west-side facility should serve neighbourhood recreation, not only elite athletes.

On road safety, councillors asked about school-zone measures after automated speed enforcement ended, and staff said temporary measures can be installed faster than permanent ones. Staff also discussed pedestrian crossover costs and agreed to look at sharing speed data with residents.
